name: Binned Raster Traversal
text:
# Binned Raster Traversal
Also called: Binned CUDA Rasterization

## Overview
Binned Raster Traversal is a GPU-accelerated rasterization method for [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) that replaces the baseline's single globally depth-sorted scan with a [linear scan](#1779-canonical-enumeration.md) over a concatenation of $K$ coarse, tile-local depth bins [S1]. It solves the performance bottleneck of global sorting by deferring depth ordering to a tile-local binning phase, allowing the rasterizer to process a contiguous memory interval without per-bin branching or complex control flow [S1]. Unlike the baseline traversal, which requires a single sorted range, this method scans the concatenated bins in front-to-back order, relying on pre-computed offsets to define the scan interval [S1].

## How it works
**Inputs:** Repaired pair stream $P$ (containing Gaussian IDs and attributes), bin offsets array `binOffsets`, optional flat-ID sidecar, Gaussian attributes (position, covariance, color, opacity), and image/tile dimensions [S1].
**Outputs:** Rendered colors $C_p$, alphas $\alpha_p$, and last contributing Gaussian IDs for each pixel $p$ [S1].

**Data Structures:**
* `binOffsets[t, k]`: An integer array of size $T \times (K+1)$, where $T$ is the number of tiles and $K$ is the number of coarse bins per tile. `binOffsets[t, k]` stores the start index in the pair stream for the $k$-th bin of tile $t$ [S1].
* **Pair Stream:** A contiguous array of Gaussian entries [S1].
* **Bin Order:** The bins are laid out in front-to-back order in the pair stream [S1].
* **Unsorted Bins:** Within a single bin, entries are not depth-sorted unless "[selective exact repair](#10281-selective-exact-repair.md)" has been applied [S1].

**Parameters:**
* $K$: Number of coarse bins per tile. Default is 64 [S1].
* **Configuration:** The default "No-GW" path uses direct-atomic tile-bin construction, warp-key grouping disabled, color staging enabled, conservative alpha culling enabled, and log-space depth binning [S1].
* **Termination Threshold:** The early-termination threshold for $T_p$ is a configurable parameter [S1].

**Pseudocode:**
> **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors.

```python
def binned_raster_traversal(P, binOffsets, K, tile_dims, profiling=False, culling_enabled=True, staging_enabled=True, termination_threshold=1e-4, batch_size=256):
    for t in range(num_tiles):
        # [S1] Determine tile pixel coordinates and skip masked tiles
        coords = get_tile_pixel_coords(t)
        if is_masked(t):
            continue
        # [S1] Initialize color accumulator Cp to 0 and transmittance accumulator Tp to 1 for all pixels p in the tile
        for p in coords:
            Cp[p] = 0.0
            Tp[p] = 1.0
        # [S1] Set the scan interval [a,b) to [binOffsets[t,0], binOffsets[t,K])
        a = binOffsets[t, 0]
        b = binOffsets[t, K]
        # [S1] Iterate through batches within the interval [a,b)
        for batch_start in range(a, b, batch_size):
            # [S1] If all pixels in the tile have terminated, break the loop
            if all_pixels_terminated(Tp, coords):
                break
            # [S1] Load candidate Gaussian IDs into shared memory
            ids = load_candidates_to_shared_memory(P, batch_start, batch_size)
            # [S1] If tile-alpha culling is enabled, remove candidates below the tile-level contribution threshold
            if culling_enabled:
                ids = cull_below_tile_alpha_threshold(ids)
            # [S1] If color staging is enabled, stage candidate colors cooperatively in shared memory
            if staging_enabled:
                colors = stage_candidate_colors_cooperatively(ids)
            # [S1] For all Gaussians g in the surviving batch order, iterate over all active pixels p in the tile
            for g in ids:
                for p in coords:
                    # [S1] If traversal profiling is enabled, count candidate visits
                    if profiling:
                        count_candidate_visit()
                    # [S1] Evaluate the same opacity/conic test as the baseline
                    alpha = evaluate_opacity_conic_test(g, p)
                    # [S1] Update Cp and Tp using baseline alpha compositing
                    Cp[p] += alpha * Tp[p] * colors[g]
                    Tp[p] *= (1.0 - alpha)
                    # [S1] If Tp reaches the early-termination threshold, mark pixel p as inactive
                    if Tp[p] < termination_threshold:
                        mark_pixel_inactive(p)
        # [S1] Write final color, alpha, and last contributing id for each pixel
        write_final_output(Cp, Tp, last_contributing_id)
```

**Formulas:**
* Opacity/conic test (baseline): $\alpha_g = \text{opacity}_g \cdot \exp(-\frac{1}{2} \mathbf{d}^T \Sigma^{-1} \mathbf{d})$ [S1]
* Alpha [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) update: $C_p \leftarrow C_p + \alpha_g \cdot T_p \cdot \text{color}_g$ [S1]
* Transmittance update: $T_p \leftarrow T_p \cdot (1 - \alpha_g)$ [S1]

**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:**
* The linear scan processes unsorted intra-bin entries in batch order, which is acceptable because the front-to-back bin layout ensures correct compositing across bins [S1].
* Selective exact repair restores exact baseline depth order within bins when needed, but does not handle cross-bin ordering as the bin layout already guarantees front-to-back progression [S1].
* The early-termination threshold for $T_p$ is a configurable parameter [S1].

## Operating characteristics
* **Time Complexity:** The rasterization loop performs a linear scan of the pair stream interval defined by the bins [S1].
* **Memory Complexity:** Requires shared memory for candidate batches and per-pixel accumulators [S1].
* **Performance:** In synthetic scale-up tests scaling the workload from 5M to 30M Gaussians, this method demonstrates consistent performance scaling on RTX 4090 hardware, avoiding the bottlenecks of global sorting [S1].
* **Strengths:** Eliminates per-bin branching in the rasterization kernel; simplifies control flow; leverages tile-locality for efficient memory access [S1].
* **Limitations:** Relies on the correctness of the preceding [tile-local bin construction](#10280-tile-local-bin-construction.md) phase; performance depends on the effectiveness of tile-alpha culling and [early termination](#4675-early-termination.md) [S1].

## Background
Binned Raster Traversal is part of the TileGS framework, which introduces tile-local depth binning for Gaussian Splatting rasterization [S1]. It was developed to address the computational cost of global depth sorting in large-scale Gaussian splatting scenes [S1]. The method builds on the baseline rasterization approach but modifies the data layout to enable efficient parallel processing on GPUs [S1].
